The manipulation of time in the story is exceptionally well-balanced and serves the narrative arc effectively. The author uses **compression of time** in the first five paragraphs, summarizing fourteen years (four years of college and ten years of post-graduate life) into a brief, witty overview. This efficiently establishes the mythos of "Q" as an untouchable, frictionless "golden boy" without bogging the story down in unnecessary chronological detail. 

Once the narrator spots Q at the beach club, the pacing shifts to **real-time and stretched time**, dedicating the bulk of the story to a single ten-minute conversation. As Q's charm begins to fail during the layoff conversation, the author stretches brief moments—such as a "three-second" pause where Q's "mechanism jammed"—by filling them with sharp sensory details (a crescent of sweat, papery skin, the *zzt* of a zipper) and the narrator's internal observations. This contrast between fourteen compressed years of effortless grace and a few stretched, agonizing minutes of failure makes the shattering of the narrator's illusion about Q feel earned and deeply impactful.
